title: 1 Thessalonians
tagline: A warm letter to a young church under pressure: hold on, love each other, and wait for the Lord's return with hope.
author: Paul
authorNote: The letter names Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy (1:1), and almost no scholar doubts that Paul wrote it; it is often counted among his earliest letters, and so among the earliest writings in the New Testament. Some scholars question whether 2:13-16 (with its harsh words about "the Jews") was written by Paul or added later, since it seems out of step with Romans 9 to 11; others defend it as Paul's own words about a particular group in a particular situation.
audience: The church in Thessalonica, mostly Gentile converts who had turned from idols
audienceNote: Paul, Silas, and Timothy founded the church on the second journey after being driven out of Philippi (Acts 16:11-40; 17:1-9). Thessalonica was the capital of the Roman province of Macedonia, a busy port city on the Via Egnatia. The church had grown quickly and was immediately under pressure from fellow townspeople (1:6; 2:14; 3:3-4).
setting: Corinth, about AD 50 to 51, only months after Paul left Thessalonica
settingNote: Paul had been forced out of Thessalonica after a short stay, went on to Athens, and then to Corinth. Worried about the new believers, he sent Timothy back; Timothy rejoined him with good news (3:1-6; Acts 18:5), and Paul wrote in reply. The letter is dated by Paul's year in Corinth and the governor Gallio (Acts 18:12). Corinth is not named in the letter; it is inferred from Acts.
genreNote: A warm, personal letter in the form of ancient correspondence: greeting, thanks, a long reminder of how Paul and his friends behaved, news and prayers, practical instruction, and a conclusion. The tone is that of a father and a nurse writing to children they miss.
bigIdea: The gospel changed the Thessalonians from idol-worshippers to people who serve the living God and wait for his Son; so keep going in faith, love, and hope, live quietly and well, and comfort one another with the promise that Christ will return and the dead in Christ will rise.
mapTitle: Map: Philippi, Thessalonica, Athens, and Corinth
mapSummary: Paul's route: beaten and jailed in Philippi, then Thessalonica, then Athens (where he sends Timothy back), and on to Corinth, where he writes.
